name: Broadsheet — Monochrome Editorial
thesis: OFFSUIT as a printed strategy broadsheet rendered in the dark: warm ink-on-paper typography, hairline rules, a strict grid, vast negative space, and light editorial serif figures for the numbers that carry weight. The premium is typographic craft and REDUCTION — every border, box, colour and label must earn its place or be cut. Three disciplines hold it and now apply identically to Home, the live Table and every drill: the page is printed in exactly TWO INKS (a warm bone and one muted red printing ink used only to encode card suits, the way a real letterpress deck is set); there is exactly ONE signal colour (a low-chroma jade ink) that never fills a shape and only marks "the thing that matters right now"; and there is ONE load-bearing serif figure size for every number that matters anywhere in the product. The live table stops being a felt object and becomes a typeset data page, and its most crafted element is the playing card — a fine-press index card with a warm-paper body, a dominant tabular rank, and one solid ink suit — so the card, not a table surface, is the beautiful object the eye rests on.
references: FT & Monocle editorial pages (broadsheet hierarchy, serif headline figures, red-ink second colour, small-caps labels, generous margins, market/standings tables); Apple Stocks & Numbers (data-as-typography, quiet dividers, no chrome) and Apple's critically-damped UIKit springs (organic arrival with no bounce); Linear (warm-dark surfaces, hairline elevation, zero glow, crisp fast micro-interactions); Vercel/Geist (grid discipline, tabular numerals, snappy ease-outs); Teenage Engineering & Braun (monochrome instrument, one small functional accent, ruthless part-count reduction, motion that never fidgets); Stripe dashboard (calm figures); fine-press minimalist playing-card decks — single-index, large-centre-figure, two-ink letterpress (black/red printing, NOT four-colour glossy casino).
